name: Brena Angelo da Silva
headline: Full Stack Developer · UX/UI Designer
summary: Full stack developer and UX/UI designer. I build web products end to end — from user research and prototyping to APIs, databases, testing and deployment — with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Node.js and PostgreSQL. Google UX Design certified and Software Engineering undergraduate. Looking for roles where design, code and user impact go together.

bullets: Built KADOSH's e-commerce end to end (faith-inspired fashion brand, retail and wholesale) with Next.js 15 (App Router), React 19 and TypeScript, including a full self-service checkout that requires no human support.
Integrated payments via PagBank (Pix and credit card, confirmed through webhooks), shipping quotes via SuperFrete (Correios, Jadlog, Loggi) and address autofill from postal code (ViaCEP).
Designed the PostgreSQL (Neon) data model with Prisma — products, variants, inventory, orders and payments — with stock reservations released automatically by a Netlify scheduled function.
Implemented an admin panel with custom authentication (scrypt password hashing and HMAC-signed session in a secure cookie) and Zod validation on every API input.
Wrote automated tests with Vitest (wholesale rules, CPF validation, webhook signatures, shipping and session) running in CI on GitHub Actions on every push; currently maintaining the project.
Designed and built Banco de Talentos in 3 weeks: a showcase with search by trade, name or product, in vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
Design and develop the website and internal system of a nonprofit that supports women who have experienced violence, using Next.js, React, Prisma and PostgreSQL (Neon, São Paulo region).
Built a restricted area where staff register and manage the people in the program — women supported, employees, board members and volunteers — with print and PDF export.
Treated privacy of sensitive data as a core requirement: access limited to authenticated staff and no internal information exposed on the public site.
Maintain the system in production, with code on GitHub and continuous deployment on Netlify.
